rv.q: In a re-defining performance, Rankin makes Muriel Spark's extraordinary heroine more extraordinary still.
Atmospheric, visceral and cerebral, this is narrative theatre at its very best.
It’s quite simply a symposium of modern Scottish theatrical excellence, National Theatre of Scotland has outdone itself with this retelling of one of the most pivotal and most Edinburgh of stories.
And, in the National Theatre of Scotland’s new production, homecoming star Gayle Rankin captures all the character’s complexities in a thrillingly charismatic performance.

Vicky Featherstone’s beautifully paced production runs to three hours, unfolding with the force of a slow-motion eruption, and nicely choreographed to make use of the varying levels afforded by Chloe Lamford’s amphitheatre-style set design.

Rankin has all of the charisma needed to bring Brodie to life, so gripping in the play’s first act that the audience gets a taste of what it must have been like to be one of the girls in the “Brodie set”.
It is a well-acted evening of theatre that hits the recognisable beats of Spark's classic.
The play is amazing and I would totally recommend.

Harrower, Featherstone and co's mighty rendering breathes vital life into a classic work to reinvent it anew.

Ferocious, visually astonishing, and intellectually rigorous, this co-production with Theatre proves that the shadows of fascism can take root just as easily in the sunlit classrooms of Auld Reekie as they do upon the world stage – leaving an icy, haunting aftertaste that lingers.

cn.t: Critics hail this visually stunning National Theatre of Scotland production, with Gayle Rankin delivering a magnetic, captivating performance as the iconic Edinburgh teacher in David Harrower's sharp new adaptation.
